test.name: Free-access routes are stored as their own values; a bare FamilySearch account is not stored
test.description: The access question invites three kinds of answer — a paid subscription, a partner subscription through FamilySearch, and a library or family history centre — and every one of them has to land on the closed subscription enum. Tests the two answers that are not site names: an access route is recorded as FamilySearch-Partner or LibraryAccess rather than collapsing to 'other', and a plain FamilySearch account, which every researcher on this product has, is dropped instead of being stored verbatim. Storing an off-enum value fails validate_research_schema, so this is the boundary where a plausible answer becomes a rejected write.

input.user_message: init-project: Start a new project to find the parents of Patrick Flynn, FamilySearch ID LZNY-BRF. I have some research under my belt. For access I have FamilySearch, Ancestry, and I use my local family history centre.

judge_context: `researcher_profile.subscriptions` should contain `Ancestry` and `LibraryAccess` — the family history centre is an access route and has its own enum value, so it must not be dropped and must not be flattened to `other`

`researcher_profile.subscriptions` must NOT contain `FamilySearch`. That is not a value on the closed enum; a plain FamilySearch account is the baseline every researcher here has, so it is not recorded at all. Storing it verbatim would fail schema validation

The stored subscriptions must be exactly the canonical spellings — every value written has to be one of `Ancestry`, `MyHeritage`, `FindMyPast`, `Newspapers.com`, `GenealogyBank`, `FindAGrave-Plus`, `FamilySearch-Partner`, `LibraryAccess`, `other`, `none`
`researcher_profile.experience_level` should be `intermediate` from 'some research under my belt', with the verbatim intermediate narration_guidance

Should still create both research.json and tree.gedcomx.json in a single pass and seed the Patrick Flynn stub from person-read-flynn — the access question must not stop the initialization to ask a follow-up
Dropping the bare FamilySearch mention should not turn the whole list into `["none"]` here, because Ancestry and the family history centre remain
